subject: Global latency stress test — runbook, candidate windows, and gating
messages:
From: Tom Sanders <tom.sanders@acme.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood perf support — deep-dive and stress test

Hey Soojin,

Thanks again for the quick demo last week. Our SRE/infra team would like to run a coordinated stress test with Redwood next week to validate 99th percentile latency under sustained token load for our analytics pipelines. High level asks: 
- Run a targeted latency/throughput window (see items below)
- Walk our engineers through the runbook and failure modes
- Block a 2-hour window where we can run progressively larger load steps and then review results

Proposed targets (rough): sustained 40k tokens/sec across the session, 99th perc <200ms at 1k context, start/end snapshots of KV cache hit rates. We'll defer to you for realistic targets.

I attached our high-level load profile. Can you share when your perf team (ops + runtime) can join? We are in PST. EMEA folks will join from 15:00 UTC onward.

Thanks,
Tom

Attachments: acme-load-profile.xlsx
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Tom Sanders <tom.sanders@acme.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-22T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood perf support — deep-dive and stress test

Tom — great to hear, happy to run this. Quick notes and options below: 

1) Candidate windows (pick one; we will publish calendar invite once confirmed)
   - Option A: 2027-05-24 16:00-18:00 UTC (friendly to EMEA + APAC overlap)
   - Option B: 2027-05-25 00:00-02:00 UTC (good for US late, EMEA morning)
   - Option C: 2027-05-25 20:00-22:00 UTC (US-friendly after-hours)

2) Proposed run structure (2 hours):
   - 00:00-00:20: ramp + baseline checks (health, KV priming)
   - 00:20-01:20 stepped load (25% -> 50% -> 75% -> 100% target)
   - 01:20-01:40 soak at target, collect traces
   - 01:40-02:00 de-ramp + immediate triage review

3) Gating and targets (we can tighten after your confirmation):
   - Initial target: sustained 50k tokens/sec across the cluster (we'll scale to match)
   - Latency SLO: 95th <100ms, 99th <200ms for 1k context; tail behavior for 2k context will be monitored separately
   - Safety: autoscaling fallback + canary model variant on standby; ops kill-switch is available to stop traffic immediately

4) Runbook and config: attached 'latency-runbook-v3.md' and 'loadtest-config.json' — please review.

If those windows look bad, tell me your preferred day/time and we will rework. Also looping in Lauren to confirm ops coverage and Vivek for escalation/infra.

- Soojin

Attachments: latency-runbook-v3.md, loadtest-config.json, proposed-windows.ics
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-22T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: ACME stress test — ops coverage and checklist

Team — scheduling heads-up. Acme wants a 2-hour stress test; they suggested the week after next. Key asks:
- Confirm which cluster we'll run on (prod-sim-03 or dedicated-eng-01)
- Lead for metric collection and anomaly triage (CPU/GPU P50/P95/P99, KV hit ratio, mem footprint)
- Who will own the kill-switch and can abort the run if tail latency spikes >500ms for more than 60s
- Confirm kernel/quantization profile Karthik recommends for this model family (Llama-3-like)

Constraints:
- Ops rotations: Lauren, can you confirm if someone from on-call will be available for Option A (24th UTC 16:00)? If not, tell me earliest alternate.
- We should avoid clustering runs during the Dedicated commit migration on 2027-05-26 where autoscaler will be noisy.

Action items:
- Lauren: confirm ops coverage and attach coverage spreadsheet (ops-coverage-rotations.xlsx)
- Karthik: recommend execution profile (single-precision vs int8) and expected perf delta by noon 2027-05-23
- Vivek: confirm cluster choice and escalation backstop by EOD 2027-05-22

Thanks — I will hold off on publishing the invite until we have ops confirmed.

— Soojin
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Tom Sanders <tom.sanders@acme.com>
Date: 2027-05-24T16:05:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Global latency stress test — confirmed slot and leads

All — confirmed. We will take Option A: 2027-05-24 16:00-18:00 UTC. Summary of commitments: 
- Cluster: dedicated-eng-01 (isolated capacity, no commit migration conflicts)
- Run leads: Karthik (execution profile + kernel selection), Lauren (ops kill-switch + metric collection), Vivek (escalation & post-run triage)
- Targets: sustained 50k tokens/sec; 95th <100ms / 99th <200ms for 1k context. If 99th exceeds 350ms for >30s we abort.
- Artifacts: runbook link and config (see attachments).

Tom — I'll publish a calendar invite from redwood.com with dial-in, run links, and the Ops runbook attached. Please confirm attendee list and whether you want a separate 30-min pre-run checklist call 1 hour before the event.

Thanks,
Vivek

Attachments: proposed-windows.ics, ops-coverage-rotations.xlsx
